title: Verifier crossing law (a) is exact-sign: a shared end a rounding apart can hold the post

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while fixing #1048.

The verifier's crossing law (a) (`crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs`, `proper_cross`, asked by `verify/crossing.rs` of every Feed-Feed chord pair of different moves at a shared depth) tests exact signs: an orientation of exactly 0 is a touch, anything else counts. Two moves that meet at one vertex reached twice, a rounding apart (an orbit closing a ulp off its start, a microlift return landing on a chord end, a ring starting on the last ring's vertex), can therefore read as a proper crossing. `Warning::Crossing` blocks the post.

The #1048 fix widens the adaptive planner's own check (`motion/.../adaptive/guard.rs`, `crosses`) to read "on the other chord's line" within `TOUCH` = 1e-9 mm. The planner now accepts such a plan where it used to fall back to Offset rings, but the verifier still uses the exact zero. If the posted moves keep a rounding-apart shared vertex, the post is held by a Crossing warning instead. That is still safe (refused by name), but the two laws should agree: the plan check is meant to be the verifier's law asked first.

Expected: law (a) reads a chord end within the same stated tolerance of the other chord's line as on it (sign 0), so its verdict matches the planner's `guard::crosses`. A real crossing still blocks. Under the safety floor (a verifier law), with a pin pair: a shared vertex 1e-12 mm apart does not warn, and a crossing a micron through still does.

Done means: a `crates/sim` verify test where two Feed moves share an end 1e-12 mm apart gives no Crossing warning; a micron crossing still does; the crossing suites and the bucketed-vs-all-pairs reference stay green.

Related: #1048, #980, #1010.
